decisions.reason: As a core bread line that has remained in the range after its launch, management would likely keep it because it fits the established bakery business, has visible market commitment, and shows no clear evidence of failure that would justify reversing course.
This premium raisin stollen is a publicly highlighted flagship with award recognition, so sunk commitment, reputational stakes, and positive external validation make withdrawal extremely unlikely.

Although it is a somewhat more niche rye variant, management would still tend to keep it because it survived the earlier portfolio pruning, uses existing bread capabilities, and the prior launch decision is easier to defend than to reverse.

Even as a seasonal product beside a stronger stollen flagship, it remains close to the firm's confectionery core and another year in the assortment increases commitment enough that management would likely continue it for another season unless results clearly disappoint.
